challenge_text: The biggest challenge I’ve experienced with the 2-2-1 modality is the very limited time to consult with my adviser and get important papers signed, especially now that I’m in my 4th year. Since we only have face-to-face classes two days a week, I often miss my adviser’s schedule, and then I lose almost a whole week waiting for the next consultation. This causes delays in my thesis revisions, feasibility study outputs, and other requirements, which increases my stress and makes me rush my work, affecting its quality. To cope with this, I try to plan my campus days very carefully. I list all the documents I need signed and the topics I want to discuss, then I prioritize seeing my adviser first thing when I arrive on campus. I also send my drafts and questions by email or message ahead of time, so my adviser can at least read them before we meet, even if the feedback is not as detailed as in person. Sometimes, I coordinate with my classmates to find out which days our instructors are usually around, so I can adjust my schedule and maximize the few face-to-face days we have. Even with these strategies, it’s still stressful, but this is how I try to stay on track despite the limitations of the 2-2-1 setup. | As a 4th-year student, my experience with the 2-2-1 blended learning setup so far is mixed with bad things and good things. This is helpful for me since I also need to save for my thesis and maybe a part-time job. But honestly, it’s also hard, especially now that I’m in my final year. People who still need to work onsite, run businesses, or use electricity at home continue to face high costs and possible outages, so the broader problem remains.
